title: Two UFC 336 Fights With No Price Yet, and What a Blind Engine Says About Them
excerpt: UFC 336 is three months out. I ran its two booked fights through an engine that never sees a market price: Morales 65% over Prates, Van 52% over Kape. Here is what it reads, how much the round count moves it, and how often it has been right this year (34 of 64).
content:
UFC 336 in Toronto is about three months away, and two of its fights are already booked. Joshua Van defends his flyweight title against Manel Kape in the main event, five rounds. Carlos Prates against Michael Morales is three rounds at welterweight.

![UFC 336: Joshua Van, Manel Kape, Carlos Prates and Michael Morales](/blog/ufc-336-blind-engine/ufc-336.jpg)

Our database has no market price stored for either fight yet. That makes them a clean test for the blind engine on CrystlQuant, the one that prices every real UFC fight without ever seeing a price. The same engine sits behind the Lab's "What if they fought" page, which takes any two active fighters, booked or not.

## The numbers

Run on 29 October 2026 at 06:05 UTC, with each fight at its booked length:

| Fight | Rounds | Engine |
|---|---|---|
| Joshua Van v Manel Kape | 5 | Van 52.1%, Kape 47.9% |
| Carlos Prates v Michael Morales | 3 | Morales 65.0%, Prates 35.0% |

Both are calls. Van's is the narrow one, by four points; Morales's is the clear one, by thirty.

## What it reads

The engine works from each fighter's own UFC bouts, with older fights counting for less. In its own history:

| Fighter | UFC wins | UFC losses | Wins inside the distance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Michael Morales | 7 | 0 | 5 |
| Carlos Prates | 7 | 1 | 7 |
| Joshua Van | 11 | 1 | 4 |
| Manel Kape | 8 | 3 | 6 |

![Michael Morales 65%, Carlos Prates 35%](/blog/ufc-336-blind-engine/prates-morales.jpg)

Prates has finished every one of his UFC wins. His last two were Leon Edwards (KO, round two, UFC 322) and Jack Della Maddalena (TKO, round three, May 2026). The engine still has him a clear underdog, because Morales has never lost: 19 and 0 as a pro, per Sherdog, and his last three wins all ended in the first round. Both men knocked out Neil Magny in round one, less than three months apart in 2024.

![Joshua Van 52%, Manel Kape 48%](/blog/ufc-336-blind-engine/van-kape.jpg)

Van and Kape share two opponents. Both stopped Bruno Silva in the third round. Both beat Brandon Royval: Van on the cards at UFC 317, Kape by knockout in the first round in December 2025. Van has won eight straight; Kape has won four. Not much daylight, and the engine still takes Van.

## Rounds move the number

Ask for the same pairs at the other length and the engine answers differently:

| Fight | At 3 rounds | At 5 rounds |
|---|---|---|
| Prates v Morales | Prates 35.0% | Prates 38.0% |
| Van v Kape | Van 52.6% | Van 52.1% |

Two extra rounds give Prates three more points. Van barely moves. If the Prates fight were ever upgraded to a main event, the engine would see a slightly closer fight.

## How much to trust it

Graded on real UFC fights this year, the blind engine has been right 34 times out of 64, as CrystlQuant's public record showed on 29 October 2026. That is 53%, and I would rather say it than hide it. The NFL version of the same idea is at 66 of 105 this season. Fighting is the hardest sport we price, and this engine is still finding its footing there.

So treat these two numbers as a starting point for an argument, not a verdict. When the market prices these fights, the gap between the two will be the interesting part, and both will be on the site.

You can run any pairing yourself in the Lab at CrystlQuant: https://crystlquant.com/lab/whatif
